text:
ashley: Morning handoff from night shift, heads up on two ongoing alerts — embedding-queue-p99 spike and tokenstore-write-errors. I left mitigations running, handing primary to devon at 09:00 PT. Quick summary: small subset of large customers seeing elevated p99 on embeddings (~1.8s -> 4.5s); tokenstore write errors ~0.9% for US-west writers.

sre-bot: [ALERT] embedding-queue-p99 spike — 09:02 UTC — p99=4.5s, rate steady, retries increased. Pager fired x2. See /runbooks/embedding-queue (runbook id: RB-112).

devon: taking primary. saw consumer restarts on consumer-A pod group at ~08:45 PT, probably due to GC spikes. I've increased consumer concurrency from 24 -> 40 and enabled backoff jitter. Will watch for 15m.

marta: noted. I added a temporary autoscale hint to the pool (min_replicas +2) and bumped prefetch windows for embeddings-encoder to 6. That should reduce tail by batching more small requests.

kevin: tokenstore write error trace: `RequestFailedError: deadlock on table token_store_txn` in us-west-2 between 08:30-08:58. I opened a DB ticket with infra and applied a short TTL workaround to reduce multi-writer contention. Monitoring DB retries now.

ashley: thanks kevin. customer impact note: three customers (ids: cust-8432, cust-9911, cust-10029) reported increased latency and occasional 5xx. I created a temporary routing policy to route those to dedicated pool (warm fallback) for the highest SLA accounts.

lia: FYI I patched the fallback rule to avoid cascading capacity pressure on dedicated. Rule: only route if estimated tokens < 2000 and request qps < 10. Also added a budget check.

devon: live commands I ran: ```bash
# increase consumer concurrency
kubectl -n embeddings set env deploy/consumer-A CONCURRENCY=40
# bump prefetch
kubectl -n embeddings set env deploy/encoder PREFETCH=6
```

marta: note from metrics: KV cache hit rate improved from 78% -> 86% after prefetch bump, but overall CPU on encoder nodes rose ~12%. Watch cpu_pressure.

kevin: DB team responded — they identified a slow migration lock edge case, rolling hotfix ETA 2h. For now I'm keeping TTL workaround and reduced write batch size on tokenstore to 10.

devon: current status at 09:25 PT: embedding p99 drifting down to 2.1s, error rate stable around 0.6%. I'm keeping extra replicas for 30 minutes then will scale down if stable.

ashley: handoff checklist for the next oncall (lia): - primary = devon until 15:00 PT, secondary = marta. - active alerts: embedding-queue-p99, tokenstore-write-errors. - mitigations in place: consumer concurrency increased, prefetch bump, temporary pool autoscale, DB TTL workaround, dedicated-route for impacted customers. - runbook refs: https://wiki.internal/runbooks/RB-112-embedding-queue and https://wiki.internal/runbooks/RB-207-tokenstore-write-errors. - logs to watch: `encoder/*.log` and `tokenstore/txn_errors`. - playbook commands included in thread above.

oncall-rotation: handing over oncall to devon now (09:00 PT). Please ack in thread.

devon: ack — I'm primary, will escalate to infra/DB if tokenstore errors >1.5% for 10m or embedding-p99 >5s. Leaving notes in incident tracker: INC-2026-emb-queue.

lia: ack. I'll cover secondary and keep an eye on customer escalations. If dedicated pool starts hitting 80% capacity, revert routing for cust-9911.

ashley: leaving a final note: if you need to roll a quick rollback please use `service-router rollback --to stable` and ping me on-call for coordinated rollout. Good luck, handing off. :coffee:
